traits: Cap up to 8 cm, conical or bell-shaped then with a broad boss, fibrous, chestnut-brown and paler at the margin, which is usually split; white veil remnants in the centre when young
Gills crowded, greyish-white then olive-brown, with finely toothed white edges
Stem up to 8 cm, cream turning browner, often thicker at the base, solid then hollow
White flesh, mild taste, strong pungent fruity smell
Broadleaf or mixed woods, at the foot of trees, especially beech, on chalky soil · spore print snuff brown
safetyNote: Toxic: muscarine (the DGfM and Wikipedia, en). Symptoms: salivation, tears, urination, diarrhoea, digestive upset and vomiting; death by respiratory failure is possible (Wikipedia, en). It has no French Wikipedia page: the text comes from Wikipedia (en) and the DGfM. Wikipedia (en) names look-alikes among other inocybes (Inocybe lacera, I. lanatodisca, I. fastigiata).
